text: Apollo was really two spacecraft. The command and service module, called Odyssey, and the lunar module, called Aquarius. In the service module sat two oxygen tanks. They supplied air to breathe, and fed the fuel cells that made the ship's electricity and water. Oxygen tank two had a hidden history. Two years earlier, it had been jolted while being removed from another spacecraft. Then, in a ground test, it wouldn't empty properly. So technicians switched on its internal heater, for hours, to boil the oxygen off. The heater's safety switches were rated for twenty-eight volts. But the ground power supply ran at sixty-five. The switches welded shut. Inside the tank, temperatures reached over five hundred degrees Celsius, and cooked the insulation on the wires.
